# bunqueue

> bunqueue is a high-performance job queue for the Bun runtime, written in TypeScript. It runs in memory or with one-file SQLite persistence by default and supports PostgreSQL 15–18 for active multi-broker fleets. It offers a BullMQ-compatible API and ships a native MCP server so AI agents can control queues directly. `msgpackr` is its only direct runtime dependency.

Key facts:
- Runs embedded (in-process memory or `bun:sqlite`) or as a standalone TCP/HTTP server (MessagePack binary protocol on port 6789, REST/WebSocket/SSE on 6790). Standalone servers may select PostgreSQL for database-authoritative multi-broker coordination.
- Production features: retries with backoff, priorities, delayed jobs, cron scheduling, Dead Letter Queue, stall detection, rate limiting, concurrency caps, webhooks (HMAC-signed), SQLite S3 backups, native TLS, OpenTelemetry.
- Workflow engine: multi-step orchestration with saga compensation, branching, parallel steps, loops, signals (human-in-the-loop), nested sub-workflows.
- Performance (native 2026-07-30 campaign): ~729K jobs/sec internal in-memory batch push, ~186K public on-disk Embedded addBulk, ~159K TCP PUSHB, ~17K TCP worker drain, and ~2.7K/~3.2K linear workflows/sec Embedded/TCP. Operations and persistence boundaries are reported separately.
- Against BullMQ 6.4.2 on Redis 8.10.2 (2026-10-25, AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D): in memory bunqueue 2.9.20 adds jobs 2.6–4x faster, drains a backlog 1.1–1.3x faster and starts delayed jobs 8.5x closer to their due time; on disk, Redis with AOF drains a backlog about 7x faster than bunqueue on SQLite. Details: https://bunqueue.dev/guide/bullmq-benchmark/
- Install: `bun add bunqueue` — import from `bunqueue/client` (Queue, Worker, FlowProducer, Bunqueue) or `bunqueue/workflow` (Workflow, Engine).

How to read these docs:
- Every page below has a plain-Markdown version for agents: append `.md` to its path (`/guide/queue/` is also served as `/guide/queue.md`). It carries the same text and code with no navigation, imports, JSX or layout HTML; tabs become bold labels (for example **Bun**, **Python**) above each language's code.
- The whole documentation is also one text file: [Full documentation text](https://bunqueue.dev/llms-full.txt).
- Queue and Worker must use the same mode: `embedded: true` on both (in-process, Bun only), or a TCP `connection` to a server on both. Without `embedded: true` a client connects over TCP to `localhost:6789`.

## Queue

- [Adding Jobs](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/adding-jobs/): Single and bulk adds, priorities, delays, per-job attempts and timeouts, durable writes that skip the buffer
- [JobOptions Reference](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/options/): Every JobOptions field with its type and default (priority, delay, attempts, backoff, timeout, jobId, removeOnComplete, durable)
- [Deduplication](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/deduplication/): Custom job ids for idempotent adds, deduplication keys with a TTL, looking up or clearing a key
- [Querying Jobs](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/querying/): Fetch a job by id, list by state, count per state and priority, read results and progress, what each state means
- [Queue Control](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/control/): Pause and resume, drain, obliterate, clean by age and state, bulk retry, promote delayed jobs
- [Progress, Logs and Dependencies](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/progress/): Progress updates, per-job logs, parent/child links created by flows
- [Rate Limits and Global Concurrency](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/limits/): Per-window rate limits, a concurrency ceiling across every worker, clearing both
- [Job Groups](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/job-groups/): Per-tenant round-robin FIFO, per-group depth, rate limits and concurrency
- [Job Schedulers](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/schedulers/): Named, updatable repeatable schedules with upsertJobScheduler
- [Workers, Stats and Metrics](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/metrics/): Registered workers, per-queue statistics, windowed metrics, event stream trimming
- [DLQ from the Queue](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/dlq/): Configure, list, retry and purge the dead letter queue; embedded vs TCP differences
- [Namespaces, Auto-Batching and Store-and-Forward](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/queue/advanced/): prefixKey isolation, transparent TCP auto-batching, forwarding local jobs to a central server

## Worker

- [Concurrency and Batch Pulling](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/worker/concurrency/): Parallel jobs, runtime concurrency changes, batch pulling and long polling
- [The Job Object](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/worker/job-object/): Data and metadata, progress, per-job logs, lock extension, child results inside a processor
- [Worker Events](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/worker/events/): completed, failed, progress, stalled, active, drained, log and closed, with payload signatures
- [Errors, Retries and Backoff](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/worker/errors/): Attempts, exponential backoff, per-job timeouts, permanent failure into the DLQ
- [Lifecycle and Graceful Shutdown](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/worker/lifecycle/): Pause, resume, and close so in-flight jobs finish instead of stalling on deploy
- [Heartbeats, Stalls and Locks](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/worker/stalls/): Heartbeats, stall recovery when a worker dies, the lock that prevents double processing
- [SandboxedWorker](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/worker/sandboxed/): Experimental isolated processing in worker threads on Bun, Node.js and Deno
- [WorkerOptions Reference](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/worker/options/): Every WorkerOptions field with its default (concurrency, batchSize, pollTimeout, heartbeatInterval, lockDuration, prefixKey)

## Scheduling, Retries & Flows

- [Cron Recipes](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/cron/recipes/): Fixed intervals, cron patterns in an IANA timezone, jobs that repeat after each completion
- [Cron Reference](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/cron/reference/): Five-field syntax and shortcuts, every repeat option with defaults and per-SDK names, cron from AI agents
- [DLQ Automatic Retry](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/dlq/auto-retry/): Bounded exponential redelivery that survives SQLite or PostgreSQL broker restarts
- [DLQ Configuration](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/dlq/configuration/): Every setDlqConfig option (automatic retry, interval, ceiling, expiry, per-queue cap) with defaults
- [DLQ Operations](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/dlq/operations/): Filter by reason or age, retry a subset, remove one entry, health counters, purge
- [DLQ Reference](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/dlq/reference/): Failure reasons, entry structure with attempt history, complete method surface
- [Flow Patterns](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/flow/patterns/): Sequential chains, fan-in parents, deeper trees, reading child results
- [Flow Failure Handling](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/flow/failures/): What a parent does when a child fails, and the four child options that change it
- [FlowProducer Reference](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/flow/reference/): Every FlowProducer method, processor-side job helpers, the shape of a flow step
- [Workflow Steps & Control Flow](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/workflow/steps/): Step context, retries with backoff, timeouts, schema validation, branching, parallel steps, loops
- [Workflow Rollback](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/workflow/rollback/): Saga compensation order, per-step outcomes, failing rollbacks, the point of no return

## Server Mode & APIs

- [Server Mode](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/server/): Standalone TCP+HTTP server, token auth, Docker, graceful shutdown
- [CLI Reference](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/cli/): push/pull/ack, queue control, DLQ, cron, stats from the terminal
- [HTTP REST API](https://bunqueue.dev/api/http/): 83 REST endpoints plus WebSocket and SSE real-time events
- [TCP Protocol](https://bunqueue.dev/api/tcp/): MessagePack wire format, length-prefixed framing, and a linked summary of every command; the full command reference is split by family (jobs, queries, control and limits, DLQ, cron, flows, monitoring, workers and webhooks)
  - [Job commands](https://bunqueue.dev/api/tcp/jobs/): PUSH, PUSHB, PUSHF, PULL, PULLB, ACK, ACKB, FAIL, job logs, lock extension
  - [Query commands](https://bunqueue.dev/api/tcp/queries/): Job by id or custom id, state, result and progress, filtered paging, counts
  - [Control commands](https://bunqueue.dev/api/tcp/control/): Cancel, update, promote, discard; pause, drain, clean; rate, concurrency and group config
  - [DLQ commands](https://bunqueue.dev/api/tcp/dlq/): List with filters, stats, retry, purge, remove, re-queue completed jobs
  - [Cron commands](https://bunqueue.dev/api/tcp/cron/): Create or update cron and interval schedules, list, read, delete
  - [Flow commands](https://bunqueue.dev/api/tcp/flows/): Parent linking, failed and ignored child values, removing child dependencies
  - [Monitoring commands](https://bunqueue.dev/api/tcp/monitoring/): Ping, hello, stats, metrics, Prometheus text, storage health, heartbeats
  - [Worker and webhook commands](https://bunqueue.dev/api/tcp/workers/): Register and list workers; add, remove and list SSRF-checked webhooks
- [API Reference by version](https://bunqueue.dev/reference/): Every exported class, interface and type, generated from the source of each release
- [TypeScript Types](https://bunqueue.dev/api/types/): Job, Queue, Worker, DLQ, and connection interfaces
- [Native TLS](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/tls/): Encrypt TCP and HTTP traffic without a reverse proxy
- [MCP Server for AI Agents](https://bunqueue.dev/guide/mcp/): 79 primary MCP tools for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf over stdio or Streamable HTTP; opt-in toolsets, destructive-call confirmation, decision models (Jev, Clef, Clef-flash, Kev 9B, Laya) and workflow approval tools

## Quick Example

```typescript
import { Queue, Worker } from 'bunqueue/client';

// Embedded mode — no server needed
const queue = new Queue('emails', { embedded: true });

await queue.add('send-welcome', { to: 'user@example.com' }, {
  attempts: 3,
  backoff: 1000,
  priority: 5,
});

// Same mode as the queue: without embedded: true the worker would connect over TCP.
const worker = new Worker('emails', async (job) => {
  await sendEmail(job.data);
  return { sent: true };
}, { embedded: true, concurrency: 10 });

worker.on('completed', (job, result) => console.log(job.id, result));
```
